text.title: GovTech FOIA / Records-Retention BA Pack — Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete pack for a state benefits intake portal, with a note on every value a reader might question, and one federal grants portal pack that breaks four subject rules and what the validator and the reviewer say about it.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: A state human-services agency is replacing a paper benefits application with a web portal. Records live in Postgres, an S3 upload bucket, CloudWatch audit logs and a SharePoint policy library; caseworkers talk in Teams and a vendor Zendesk. The state's public-records clock is 10 working days. The BA runs steps 1-9 of `content/04-procedure.xml` over two weeks and hands the launch board the pack below.

section.title: Good example: state benefits intake portal

example.title: Complete pack, one open blocker
example.note: `access_request_clock_working_days` is 10, not 20: the state act sets its own clock and the contract only pins 20 for us-federal and uk. Every store's lead time sits under 10; SharePoint is the slowest at 5 because eDiscovery runs overnight.

`postgres.case_notes.body` is manual-review with a cost estimate rather than field-driven: the notes column mixes applicant PII with non-exempt case narrative and cannot be split without a data-model change the agency deferred. The 40-hour figure is what the access officer will quote when scoping a request.

`program policy decisions` is the one class with disposition transfer-to-archives: it is the only class with permanent historical value under the state schedule; everything citizen-facing is destroyed after its period.

Clause C-21 is waived, so `waived_by` names the procurement officer; the contract refuses a waiver without a person. C-7.1 is open, so it appears in both the log and `blocking_findings` — the launch board sees it once at the top.

`public_notice.buffer_days` is 120 against a minimum of 90: the state APA comment period is 45 days but the agency's rules committee meets monthly, so the BA reserved the review time the rule asks for on top of the notice.
Both officers are `role:handle` persons. The records officer signed on 2026-02-20, before any delete job was scheduled, which is the order step 8 of the procedure requires.

example.title: Four subject rules broken
example.note: What the validator prints: `record_classes[0].disposition: 'retain indefinitely' not in allowed enum` (r-retention-schedule-per-record-class); `data_stores[0].export_lead_time_working_days: 45 is above maximum 20` because jurisdiction is us-federal (r-request-export-within-statutory-clock); `exemption_map[0]: missing required field: manual_review_cost_estimate` (r-exempt-fields-tagged-in-schema); `staff_channels[0].capture_mechanism: length 0 is under minLength 5` on an auto-deleting channel (r-ephemeral-channels-captured); `accessibility_audit.level: 'A' is not the required const 'AA'`, `manual_tests: 1 items is under minItems 3`, `launch_gate: 'post-launch-review'` and a missing statement URL (r-wcag-aa-audit-gates-launch); six clause topics missing from `clause_review_log` (r-procurement-clause-review-log); `public_notice.buffer_days: 30 is below minimum 90` and `notices_filed: 0 items` (r-public-notice-buffer-scheduled).

What the reviewer sees beyond the validator: the Kafka topic holds responsive records with a 45-day custom export and an "eng:platform" owner, yet `blocking_findings` is empty — the pack hides its own worst finding. Launch on 2026-05-01 is inside any PRA window that has not even started; under 44 U.S.C. §3507 the form cannot collect without an OMB control number. The reviewer returns the pack at step 2 of the procedure.

list.item: The clock is per jurisdiction, so the contract pins 20 only where the statute does; a state pack that copied 20 from a federal template would have shipped a wrong SLA.
Manual-review rows are legitimate only with a cost estimate; the estimate is what turns "we will redact by hand" into a number the access officer can plan around.
An open clause that is not echoed in `blocking_findings` is invisible to the launch board; the summary list exists so nobody has to read the whole log.
